To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a reproducible experimental workflow can facilitate the discovery of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets in human samples undergoing degenerative processes; (2) the identification and experimental manipulation of these targets could lead to the development of novel therapies; (3) proteomic analysis of human MD samples can identify novel biomarkers and targets for therapeutic intervention.
proteomic experimentation can be a powerful tool for identifying molecular perturbations in disease models, and can also be used to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets in patient samples.

proteomic techniques offer insights to the molecular perturbances in muscular dystrophies and revisiting published datasets can identify conserved downstream molecular changes which may be worth investigating for therapeutic potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms driving neurodegenerative diseases.
the molecular consequences of MDs and the development of novel therapeutic interventions.
the development of a workflow that can efficiently identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets in complex human samples undergoing neurodegeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of both approaches is required to identify the most promising targets for therapeutic development.
proteomics is a powerful tool for understanding disease, and that the most important aspect of proteomics research is the quality of the experimental paradigm.
proteomic experimentation has the potential to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets, but only if the experimental design and data processing are carefully considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proteomic analysis of human samples is an effective method for identifying biomarkers, but the most promising targets for therapeutic intervention are likely to be conserved across disease types and are best studied using model systems.
a well-designed experimental paradigm can provide mechanistic insights, which may offer therapeutic targets and/or biomarkers for disease diagnosis and monitoring.

the proteome of a disease can be used to identify biomarkers, therapeutic targets and disease specific degenerative cascading processes, but only if the experimental paradigm is designed and executed appropriately.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proteomic analysis of patient samples can be a powerful tool for understanding the molecular perturbances occurring in MD and other neurodegeneratives, and that this can be achieved through a reproducible and efficient workflow.

the use of proteomics in human MD samples can provide valuable insights into disease pathophysiology, and that a well-designed experimental workflow can be used to generate a comprehensive list of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
a well planned experimental paradigm is essential to ensure that the data generated are of sufficient quality for meaningful interpretation.
